sources.note: Introduces GSM8K, 8.5K grade-school math word problems, and shows that training a verifier to rank many sampled solutions beats finetuning the generator directly.
sources.title: Training Verifiers to Solve Math Word Problems

sources.note: Shows that reasoning ability can be incentivized in an LLM by pure reinforcement learning on verifiable tasks, with no human-annotated reasoning trajectories, and that the resulting reasoning patterns can be transferred to smaller models.
sources.title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning

sources.note: A training-free two-stage prompting protocol that extracts a problem's answer-space constraints first and then checks its own intermediate and final results against them, routed on by a regex detector.
sources.title: Constraint-First Reasoning: A Training-Free Protocol for Exploiting Answer-Space Constraints in Mathematical Problem Solving

sources.note: Tests whether systems that translate natural-language reasoning steps into Lean preserve invalidity as well as validity, by automatically perturbing steps to make them wrong, and finds pervasive silent correction -- with the systems best at preserving valid inputs the most likely to repair invalid ones.
sources.title: FaithformBench: Benchmarking Faithfulness of Mathematical Chain-of-Thought Autoformalisation

sources.note: Fixes reward hacking in hybrid thinking/non-thinking RL by setting per-query token limits for non-thinking responses derived from the solution part of that query's thinking responses.
sources.title: Thinking-Based Non-Thinking: Solving the Reward Hacking Problem in Training Hybrid Reasoning Models via Reinforcement Learning

sources.note: A financial reasoning benchmark built from parameterized symbolic templates with executable Python, giving machine-verifiable step-level ground truth and contamination-free regeneration.
sources.title: FinChain: A Symbolic Benchmark for Verifiable Chain-of-Thought Financial Reasoning

sources.note: Verifies correctness without training by comparing a reasoning trace's start-to-end hidden-state delta against two class centroids built from labelled experience.
sources.title: Your Reasoning Model is Secretly a Reward Model - Optimization-Free Verification from Experience

sources.note: Detects reasoning hallucinations by measuring how strongly cross-step attention routing aligns with hidden-state semantic proximity, finding that higher alignment means higher hallucination risk.
sources.title: RFS-Guard: Detecting Reasoning Hallucinations via Cross-Phase Routing Focus in Large Reasoning Models

sources.note: Benchmarks multimodal models on detecting and categorizing errors in K-12 math solutions collected from real student interactions, with the best model about 10% behind human experts.
sources.title: ErrorRadar: Benchmarking Complex Mathematical Reasoning of Multimodal Large Language Models Via Error Detection

sources.note: Shows evaluator accuracy improves monotonically with reasoning tokens spent, and that buying compute at evaluation time can substitute for buying it at generation time.
sources.title: Scaling Evaluation-Time Compute with Reasoning Models as Evaluators

sources.note: Keeps the LLM as the reasoner while a symbolic solver supplies a Logic-Augmented Context, so conflicts flagged by execution direct attention to violated constraints instead of replacing deduction.
sources.title: MAC-Reasoner: A Multi-Agent Collaborative Framework for Enhancing Logical Reasoning in Large Language Models

sources.note: A 4B small reasoning model that classifies document-claim pairs as grounded or hallucinated for RAG pipelines and produces evidence-grounded justifications.
sources.title: HalluGuard: Evidence-Grounded Small Reasoning Models to Mitigate Hallucinations in Retrieval-Augmented Generation

sources.note: Fits a structural causal model over the units of a single chain-of-thought trace using leave-one-out interventions and linear regression, producing a pairwise influence matrix between every pair of steps at a cost linear in the number of units.
sources.title: Local Causal Attribution of Chain-of-Thought Reasoning

sources.note: Replaces uniform test-time compute allocation with a training-free agent that picks reasoning tools, a search strategy and an exploration parameter per problem, using a process reward model both to prune within a trajectory and to select across iterations.
sources.title: What If We Allocate Test-Time Compute Adaptively?

sources.note: Proves that parameterizing an outcome reward as the log-likelihood ratio between a policy and a reference model makes the per-step Q value fall out of the same model for free, so a process reward model can be obtained by training an outcome reward model on response-level labels alone.
sources.title: Free Process Rewards without Process Labels

sources.note: Gives two aggregation algorithms whose failure probability provably decays to zero as inference compute grows, assuming only that the model can sometimes be right and can compare two solutions better than chance.
sources.title: Provable Scaling Laws for the Test-Time Compute of Large Language Models

sources.note: Shows that base models win pass@K on mathematics by producing wrong chains that land on right answers, and that scoring the chain too — CoT-Pass@K — reverses the verdict in RLVR's favour at every K.
sources.title: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards Implicitly Incentivizes Correct Reasoning in Base LLMs

instructions:
Write the wiki definition for 'verification'.

The sources below are every archived paper and talk that mentions it. Define it as they use it: if they disagree, say so; if the term is used loosely, say that too.

`related` is the one part of the note nothing can work out on its own. The wiki already links entities that turn up in the same summary; what it cannot see is the neighbour a reader would actually want next — the generation before this one, the benchmark it was built to beat, the method it replaces. Name those. Leave the list empty rather than repeating what the sources already put side by side.

Rules:
- Write in en.
- Ground every statement in the supplied material. If something is not stated,
  leave the field empty rather than inferring it.
- No marketing language. Prefer the specific number over the adjective.
- Return one JSON object matching the schema exactly. No prose around it.

aliases: string - other names the sources use for the same thing
output_schema.definition: string - two to four sentences defining the entity as the cited sources use it, not as a textbook would
output_schema.kind: string - one of: concept, method, dataset, model
related: string - name of a neighbouring entity worth linking to. Kept as you give it and never derived away, so name what a reader should turn to next rather than what happens to appear alongside this. Answering again replaces the whole list; an empty list retracts

result.definition: Checking whether an output is correct, and across 17 sources the capability that makes everything else in this archive possible -- the reward that trains, the selector that picks, the judge that scores. The archive's oldest source establishes the pattern by training a verifier to rank sampled solutions and finding it beats finetuning the generator directly. What the corpus adds is a catalogue of where verification is weaker than it appears. It is often evaluated only on correct inputs, so nothing measures what happens when the input is wrong -- which one source names as precisely the case of interest, since an error is what verification exists to catch. A binary verifier conflates format with content, so the policy cannot learn which it is being punished for. An imperfect verifier makes best-of-N decay with scale, as adversarial solutions that fool it become more likely to be found. And where a model does the verifying, the archive's judge material applies in full. The corpus's positive direction is verification grounded outside the model: executing generated SQL against the source table, checking a stated formula with an external checker, extracting answer-space constraints and testing intermediate results against them, or generating benchmarks from executable trees so answers are correct by construction.
